text:
Connor McDavid has not had a quiet night yet. Seventeen games, a point in every one, 44 in all (10 goals, 34 assists), with 20 of them on the power play. The Toronto Star ran a column this week with his name in the headline beside the phrase "harder to be an NHL goalie," and nobody in a crease would argue.

Some of this will cool. He's shooting 22% after 16% last season, and Edmonton has scored 16.5 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. That's the luck. The rest isn't: the Oilers take 60% of the expected goals (the quality of their chances) at five on five when he plays, Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 68% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey rated him the most valuable forward in the league in 2025-26.

Our range has him finishing between 144 and 182 points. Even the low end would be a career year for almost anyone else. The thing to watch is the goal column: if the shooting drifts back to normal, the assists alone keep him on top.
headline: Seventeen games, seventeen nights on the scoresheet
